The right-most label of a domain name conveys the top-level domain.
In www.example.com, the top-level domain is com.
The hierarchy of domains descends from the right label to the left label in the name.
Each label to the left specifies a subdivision, or subdomain, of the domain to its right.
The label example specifies the node example.com as a subdomain of the com domain.
The label www creates www.example.com, a subdomain of example.com.
Each label may contain from 1 to 63 octets.
The empty label is reserved for the root node.
When fully qualified, the root node is expressed as the empty label terminated by a dot.
The full domain name may not exceed a total length of 253 ASCII characters in its textual representation.
When using a single character per label, the limit is 127 levels.
127 characters plus 126 dots have a total length of 253.
In practice, some domain registries may have shorter limits.
A hostname is a domain name that has at least one associated IP address.
The domain names www.example.com and example.com are also hostnames.
The com domain is not a hostname.
Other top-level domains, particularly country code top-level domains, may have an IP address.
If another top-level domain has an IP address, it is also a hostname.
Hostnames impose restrictions on the characters allowed in the corresponding domain name.
A valid hostname is also a valid domain name.
A valid domain name may not necessarily be valid as a hostname.
